title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July
partialText: The trade deficit bounced back up last month as spending on data centers to feed the A.I. boom drove up imports.

title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
partialText: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the US war with Iran.

title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
partialText: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.

title: Schools Giving Aid to Minority Students Could Lose Tax Exemptions Under Trump’s New Rules
partialText: The Treasury Department released rules that would prevent schools with race-based programs from qualifying for tax-exempt status, a threat to both higher education and other private schools.

title: Trump’s D.C. Makeover Projects Are ‘Only an Idea,’ Until They’re Much More
partialText: A proposed garden of heroes is following a familiar path in which facts on the ground move faster than the courts and others can keep up.

title: Lake Ontario Is One of Many Bodies of Water Caught in a Naming Fight
partialText: President Trump’s bid to call it ‘Lake America’ stands out in a world full of contested place names, which often represent deeper political or territorial disputes.

title: Gloria Steinem, Personification of the Feminist Movement, Dies at 92
partialText: She challenged sexist assumptions, helping women develop a sense of self-worth and gain a measure of equality at work, at home and in society at large.

title: Gloria Steinem’s Glamour Was a Means to an End
partialText: The glasses, the hairdo, the bell bottoms and hip-slung belts were all wrapped up in her feminist cause.

title: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and Others Pay Tribute to Gloria Steinem
partialText: After Ms. Steinem’s death at 92, celebrities and politicians reflected on her decades of activism for women’s rights and equality.

title: Federal Prosecutors Charge ICE Agent With Lying About Minnesota Shooting
partialText: The charges are a rare instance of President Trump’s Justice Department accusing a federal agent of breaking the law while on the job.

title: ICE Skipped Basic Checks in Rush for Recruits, Whistle-Blower Says
partialText: An official who oversaw the vetting of ICE recruits cited an “unprecedented lowering of standards” amid a hiring surge.

title: Reading Jonathan Franzen’s ‘The Corrections,’ 25 Years Later
partialText: Jonathan Franzen’s novel, which put a Midwestern family under the microscope, came out a week before 9/11. Why are we still talking about it?

title: Clancy’s Lawyer, Kevin Reddington, Became a Hero to Her Supporters
partialText: The themes present in Lindsay Clancy’s trial are not unfamiliar to Mr. Reddington, a veteran defense lawyer.

title: For Russia and Ukraine, an Escalating Spiral With No End in Sight
partialText: Each side is using missiles and drones to try to pound the other into giving up, breeding ceaseless human suffering. But there is no sign that either country’s determination will weaken.

title: Rival Ukrainian Intelligence Units Open Fire Against Each Other in Kyiv
partialText: President Volodymyr Zelensky described the shootout on the streets of the Ukrainian capital as an “absolutely shameful event” and ordered an investigation.

title: El-Sayed Wants to Mend Ties With Jewish Democrats, but Some Are Still Not Impressed
partialText: Lingering concerns about the Senate nominee in Michigan could make it harder for him to assemble a winning coalition.

title: After Trump Rift, Musk Begins Spending to Boost Republicans
partialText: Mr. Musk plans to spend at least $100 million in more than a dozen competitive House and Senate races. The tech billionaire helped Donald Trump to victory in 2024.

title: The Start-Up That Helps People Die
partialText: Medical aid in dying is now legal in New York. A team of clinical professionals decided to create a practice to help their clients die on their own terms.

title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
partialText: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
partialText: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.

title: Why the Courts Are Hesitant to Punish Tech Giants Like Meta and Google
partialText: After finding antitrust violations, federal courts have been reluctant to impose harsh sanctions. They fear meddling in markets where technology is racing ahead.

title: What Did Jurassic Forests Sound Like? Like This.
partialText: Scientists spent over a decade reconstructing the calls of nine species of ancient insects to create the first accurate Jurassic soundscape.

title: MAGA Is Feeding a Separatist Surge in Canada
partialText: Drawing inspiration from MAGA, separatists in Alberta are pushing for a break away from Canada.

title: What Happened When Gloria Steinem Was 22, Pregnant and Fleeing Her Old Life
partialText: Gloria Steinem got to be who she was because of a pre-Roe abortion.

title: Pete Hegseth’s Military
partialText: We look at the department during his tenure.

title: Tell Us How You Observe Yom Kippur
partialText: Yom Kippur, which starts this year on Sept. 20, is one of the most widely observed Jewish holidays. If you are Jewish, we want to know how you experience it.

title: Travis Kelce’s New Ohio Home Has Neighbors Buzzing With Excitement About Taylor Swift
partialText: The wealthy enclave of Bratenahl, Ohio, has been aflutter after learning that Travis Kelce purchased a Lake Erie mansion.
